etymologies.etymologyHTML: Synchronically equivalent to tight +‎ -en. From Middle English tighten, from Old English tyhtan, thus originally unrelated to tight (Old English *þiht).

quote.citation: 1760, Francis Fawkes, Works of Anacreon, Sappho, Bion, Moschus, and Musæus translated into English by a gentleman of Cambridge:
quote.text: Just where I please, with tighten;d rein / I'll urge thee round the dusty plain.

definitions.definition: (economics) To make money harder to borrow or obtain.
